global_layoffs.description: Oracle's global workforce was reported to be approximately 21,000 lower year over year as the company pursued restructuring and an expensive AI data-center buildout, with the company attributing part of the decline to AI deployment.
global_layoffs.source: Oracle regulatory filing coverage via Yahoo Finance

global_layoffs.description: Apple reportedly cut roles in its Intelligent Systems Experience group, which works on AI systems used in Apple devices, but no reliable public figure for the number of affected employees was reported.
global_layoffs.source: Bloomberg coverage summarized by Yahoo Tech

global_layoffs.description: Uber announced approximately 3,300 job cuts, or 10% of its workforce, in a restructuring linked to efficiency pressures and the rising threat of robotaxis, while AI-related efficiency investments were also reported as a factor in the broader cost program.
Oracle eliminated 546 positions in its America Cloud Infrastructure business, with data-center maintenance and servicing roles most affected during the company's AI-driven infrastructure expansion.

ai_workforce_signals.headline: Autonomous AI work expected to double by 2027
ai_workforce_signals.description: An ISG study reported that less than 7% of AI-enabled work is currently performed autonomously, while companies expect the share to approach 13% by the end of 2027. The study also found that 48% of organizations classified as AI value realizers had reduced their workforce and 65% were redesigning roles.

ai_workforce_signals.headline: AI cited in one-third of 2026 tech layoff events
ai_workforce_signals.description: Crunchbase reported that AI was cited in 33% of technology layoff events in 2026, compared with 1% in 2024. Its tracker attributed 92,913 global layoffs, or 72% of the year's total, to AI, although these figures depend on the methodology used to classify AI involvement.

ai_workforce_signals.headline: IBM CHRO research highlights workforce redesign
ai_workforce_signals.description: IBM research reported that only 26% of organizations clearly define work as human-led, AI-assisted, or AI-executed. The study also found that 60% of employees worry AI is eroding their skills, while critical thinking and human judgment are increasingly valued by HR leaders.
ai_workforce_signals.source: SiliconANGLE reporting on IBM Institute for Business Value research

ai_workforce_signals.headline: Gartner projects rehiring of some AI-displaced workers
ai_workforce_signals.description: Gartner projected that 30% of employees laid off because of AI replacement may need to be rehired by 2029, potentially at higher cost. The forecast indicates that workforce reductions based solely on assumed AI substitution may create capability gaps.
ai_workforce_signals.source: CIO coverage of Gartner research via HCAMag

ai_workforce_signals.headline: Texas job postings show measurable exposure effect
ai_workforce_signals.description: A Dallas Fed analysis reported that firms with greater exposure to generative-AI automation had reduced job postings by roughly 5% to 6% by mid-2024 and 8% to 9% by early 2026. The analysis estimated that automation exposure lowered total Texas job postings by approximately 1.8% in 2024 and 2.6% in 2025.
ai_workforce_signals.source: Dallas Fed analysis summarized by Quasa

ai_workforce_signals.headline: AI workforce impact remains limited in Deloitte survey
ai_workforce_signals.description: Deloitte's 2026 State of AI in the Enterprise report identified the AI skills gap as the largest barrier to integration and found that education, rather than role or workflow redesign, was the leading workforce response. The result suggests that reskilling remains more common than direct job elimination in surveyed organizations.

weekly_stats.notable_trend: AI-related workforce reporting is increasingly focused on role redesign and autonomous-work adoption, while the most substantial documented cuts in the available coverage remain broader restructuring programs rather than layoffs explicitly attributed solely to AI.
